abstract: Anthropic's Economic Index report on learning curves, published March 24, 2026, analyzes Claude usage patterns from February 5-12, 2026. The report finds that Claude.ai tasks have become less concentrated, with the top 10 tasks declining from 24% to 19% of conversations. Personal use increased from 35% to 42% while coursework fell from 19% to 12%. High-tenure users (6+ months) demonstrate a 10% higher conversation success rate compared to newer users, identifying a learning-by-doing effect that persists even after controlling for task type and country. Users strategically select models based on task complexity: Opus usage increases 1.5 percentage points per $10 in hourly task wage on Claude.ai, with API users showing roughly double this sensitivity (2.8pp). Software developers use Opus 34% of the time versus tutors at 12%. Geographic analysis shows US adoption convergence slowing, with the timeline for equal state-level adoption extending from 2-5 years to 5-9 years. Global concentration increased, with the top 20 countries rising from 45% to 48% of per-capita usage. The report identifies potential skill-biased technological change, where early-adopting high-skill workers gain disproportionate productivity advantages.
keyFindings: About 49% of jobs have seen at least a quarter of their tasks performed using Claude, indicating broad occupational penetration.
High-tenure users (6+ months) have a 10% higher success rate than newer users, demonstrating significant learning-by-doing effects.
Users strategically select models by task complexity: Opus usage rises 1.5pp per $10 in task wage on Claude.ai, 2.8pp on API.
Early adopters with high-skill tasks have more successful interactions, identifying a channel through which skill-biased transformation may already be unfolding.
Geographic adoption convergence is slowing: timeline for equal US state-level adoption extended from 2-5 years to 5-9 years.
methodology: Privacy-preserving analysis of 1 million conversations across Claude.ai and first-party API during February 5-12, 2026, three months after Claude Opus 4.5's release. Tasks mapped to O*NET occupational classifications with wage data from Bureau of Labor Statistics. Success rates, tenure effects, and model selection patterns analyzed with controls for task type, country, and user characteristics.
qualifiers: Analysis is limited to Claude users and cannot be generalized to all AI tool usage. The one-week observation window may not capture seasonal or cyclical patterns. Success rate measurement depends on Anthropic's internal classification of 'successful' conversations, which is not independently validated. The sample reflects Anthropic's user base, which skews toward certain occupations and geographies. Anthropic has a commercial interest in demonstrating productive AI usage.
